html:
SMTO-LLM-0004 — Model server connection was reset

GUID: 3fa78a48-31e8-4884-ab74-fb1f710a63e0
Slug: llm-connection-reset
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • The connection to the model was cut off suddenly while SMTO was waiting for the answer. The part already received wasn't used, because it isn't a complete answer.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the Main card and select Check saved model. A quick check shows whether the model server is answering again or keeps dropping connections.
  2. If the check fails or this keeps happening, ask the person who runs the model server to look at its log around the time of the error. The server may have crashed or restarted, or a network device between you may be cutting long connections.
  3. When the check passes, start a new task or send your request again. Don't redo steps the earlier task already finished. Only the model's unfinished answer was lost; finished steps have already taken effect.

What success looks like

  • Check saved model passes and a new task gets a complete answer.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the time it happened, to the person who manages the model server. Don't turn off security checks to keep the connection open.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An established connection to the model endpoint was forcibly reset (ECONNRESET) before the response completed; the provider, a proxy or the network may have caused it.

What this means

  • An established connection was forcibly reset. The reset identifies a transport interruption, but does not establish whether the provider, an intermediary or the network caused it. Received fragments do not by themselves form a valid completed decision.

Why this can happen

  • The provider or an intermediary may have closed the connection abruptly; the transport exception cannot identify which one.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare provider and proxy connection logs at the failure time. A matching provider restart differs from a proxy reset with no provider interruption.

How to fix it

  • Compare provider, proxy or load-balancer logs at the failure time for crashes, restarts, idle or size limits, then send a small test with Check saved model once the connection is stable. If the provider restarted from memory pressure, reduce its load or context size before retrying.
  • Have the provider operator compare provider and proxy logs at the failure time, then test a small model request after the connection is stable.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A subsequent model response reaches its expected end without a reset.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Typed transport exception (or exact legacy standard reason where supported); no tool outcome is inferred from connection state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
